fatal_errors: The proposed Al-or-Cr alloying does not reconstruct the hydride-ink printing, hydrogen de-binding, getter-assisted vacuum sintering, quenching, and silicide-based oxidation-protection strategy.
It gives two alternative alloying elements rather than one defined intervention.
No exposure duration, mechanical-loading range, or direct test that useful tensile or high-temperature strength is retained is specified.
The assumed formation of a continuous Al2O3 or Cr2O3 scale at 5–10 at.% is unsupported and may not occur in this multicomponent refractory alloy.
No prior evidence is cited, and the falsification experiment uses an undefined 'property of interest' rather than quantitative oxidation and mechanical measurements.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies selective formation of a slow-growing oxide as a general route to improved oxidation resistance and selects a relevant 1000 °C air exposure. However, it is only a generic alternative and provides no evidence that dilute Al or Cr will generate a continuous protective scale in HfNbTaTiZr or preserve its phase constitution and mechanical performance. It misses the target processing route, controlled oxygen content, quench-dependent beta-BCC stabilization, silicide coating, quantitative oxidation-rate reduction, and phase/densification boundaries. A discriminating experiment would require fixed composition and exposure time, mass-gain kinetics and scale characterization, plus matched tensile or compression tests before and after oxidation.
